newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cuts beef export refunds.
newsitem.headline: EU cuts beef export refunds.

text.p: European Union beef export refunds were cut by 7.5 percent from midnight on Tuesday, European Commission spokesman Gerard Kiely said on Wednesday.
The cut, which is due to the strengthening U.S. dollar and a rush of applications for export licences, was made under the Commission's own powers.

It follows a 10 per cent, across-the-board reduction in refunds in January and an eight per cent cut in refunds for beef exported to South Africa in February after complaints that the local market was being distorted.
Applications for licences were reopened on Wednesday after being suspended on Monday and Tuesday. Licence applications were also suspended on Thursday and Friday of last week.
The Commission awarded licences totalling 17,950 tonnes on March 17,18 and 19 and a further 30,000 tonnes mainly from Germany on March 20 and 21.
The Commission has now awarded a total of more than 933,800 tonnes of its annual GATT quota of 1,191,800 tonnes which lasts until June 30.
The remaining 258,000 tonnes is equivalent to a limit of 18,400 a week if licence awards are to be available until the end of June, Kiely said.
"Since the last refund adjustment in January the U.S. dollar has increased by about five percent which neutralises the impact on EU traders of the 7.5 per cent, across-the-board reduction," he added.
He said that the action was taken to avoid speculative licence applications. "We wanted to avoid a situation developing in which a market in beef export licences might develop," he explained.

Earlier this year the Commission reduced the validity period for export licences to 30 days from 60 in an attempt to balance demand but a large gap between availability and demand has remained, Kiely said.
"We have a fixed annual quota for subsidised exports and if we do not ensure orderly exports through the year we would end up with a problem in May and June," he added.

The subsidised exports so far this year (July to June) include 96,500 of beef at slaughter weight (approximately 346,000 tonnes of live animals), 309,300 tonnes of fresh and chilled meat, 464,000 tonnes of frozen, 62,700 tonnes of canned and preserved beef and 1,200 tonnes of salted beef.
